label: TMUA 2021 · Paper 1 · Question 20

hints.title: Record the logarithm domains first
hints.body: Each original logarithm needs a strictly positive argument. Write all those restrictions before combining the logarithms.
hints.recap: Algebraic simplification must preserve the domain of every original logarithm.
hints.pitfall: The expression inside the logarithm is required to be positive, not merely nonzero.
hints.pause: Turn each positivity restriction into an inequality in the coordinates.

recall.reminder: Algebraic simplification must preserve the domain of every original logarithm.

hints.title: Identify the underlying curve
hints.body: Use the logarithm laws to combine each side, equate the positive arguments and expand. Then complete the square in both coordinates if the resulting equation suggests a circle.
hints.recap: The equation of a circle can be hidden behind logarithmic algebra.
hints.pitfall: Keep the domain inequalities alongside the new equation; the whole algebraic curve may not satisfy the original logarithms.
hints.pause: Find the centre and radius of the curve described by the algebraic equation.

recall.reminder: The equation of a circle can be hidden behind logarithmic algebra.

hints.title: Apply the domain to the circle
hints.body: Draw the boundary lines of your inequalities on the circle. Find where the relevant line meets the circle and use the radii to those points to determine the allowed central angle.
hints.recap: An arc length is the radius multiplied by its central angle in radians.
hints.pitfall: Choose the arc satisfying all of the original inequalities, rather than automatically using a full circumference.
hints.pause: Identify the permitted arc, find its central angle and calculate its length.

recall.reminder: An arc length is the radius multiplied by its central angle in radians.

solution:
1. Preserve the logarithm domains. We need x−y>0, 2−2x>0 and y+5>0, or x>y, x<1, y>−5.

2. Combine and rearrange. The logarithm equation gives (x−y)2=(2−2x)(y+5). Expanding and cancelling the mixed terms gives x2+y2+10x−2y=10, hence (x+5)2+(y−1)2=36. The centre is (−5,1) and the radius is 6.

3. Select the allowed arc. The circle touches x=1 at (1,1) and y=−5 at (−5,−5). The line x=y meets the circle at exactly these points. The radii to them are horizontal rightwards and vertical downwards, so the minor arc has angle π/2. It is the arc with x>y; its interior also satisfies x<1 and y>−5. The remaining arc has x<y and is excluded.

4. Find its length. The allowed arc therefore has length 6·π2=3π. Its endpoints are excluded by the logarithm domains, which does not change the arc length.

Answer D. On this domain, both original log arguments and x−y are positive, so the rearrangement introduces no extra points on the retained arc.
knowledgePattern: Convert a logarithmic locus to a circle and retain the domain-selected arc
